title: The Physical AI Scope Test
summary: Work through The Physical AI Scope Test.

blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **The Physical AI Scope Test**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol IV, The Causal Boundary, § The Physical AI Scope Test
blocks.md: A robotic arm in a fulfillment center can follow a fixed motion profile under a proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller (a classical hand-tuned feedback law that corrects in proportion to the present error, its accumulated sum, and its rate of change). It can also execute an offline trajectory pre-screened and loaded by a human technician, or stream joint torques directly from a learned policy running on real-time sensor frames. While all three regimes actuate identical electric motors and gear trains, they impose different architectural obligations on the computing system.

blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: A system is physical AI only when it has a learned statistical model, consequential physical feedback, and delegated authority at once; an independent deterministic veto does not remove delegated authority, while per-command human approval does.

questions.q: The section **The Physical AI Scope Test** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Work delivered across the causal boundary has no checkpoint to restore, so recovery is a new constrained motion limited by torque, friction, and drive limits, and the permission path must confirm that a feasible recovery still exists before it admits an action.

A system is physical AI only when it has a learned statistical model, consequential physical feedback, and delegated authority at once; an independent deterministic veto does not remove delegated authority, while per-command human approval does.

Because physical authority is state-dependent, environmental change, sensor spoofing, and post-incident reconstruction all reduce to three demands on the permission path: fresh authenticated physical state, deterministic authority to intervene with a feasible fallback, and synchronized causal telemetry.

Moving from advisory prediction through software agency to physical embodiment removes elastic virtual time, transactional rollback, and batchable execution, so data, compute, evaluation, and deployment each acquire physical stakes.
